text: I need an AI engineer skill that helps my team design RAG systems and evaluate LLM features.
something to help with our AI stuff

We are a 6-person startup building a support chatbot on top of an LLM. I want a skill that acts like a senior AI engineer for Codex: it should help us pick models and embeddings, design retrieval over our help-centre articles, write evaluation sets, and warn us about cost and prompt-injection risks before we ship.
Make a skill that reviews pull requests for bugs, security problems and readability.
can you make something that checks my code

I want a Codex skill that reviews diffs the way our senior engineers do: first understand what the change is for, then look for real bugs and security holes, then maintainability. Comments must be ranked (blocking, should fix, nit), point to exact lines and suggest a fix. It must not nitpick formatting that our linter already handles.
Create a data analyst skill that writes SQL, analyses spreadsheets and explains results to managers.
I want help with my numbers

Our sales team exports CSVs from the CRM every week and nobody trusts the numbers. I want a skill that behaves like an experienced data analyst: it should check the data for problems first, write the pandas or SQL code, pick the right chart, and explain what the result means and how sure we can be, in plain language for the sales director.
Create a skill that explains blood test results to patients in plain language.
something to understand my health papers

Patients at our clinic get their lab results online days before they see a doctor and call us worried. I want a skill that explains what each value measures and what the reference range means, in plain language, helps them write questions for their appointment, and always tells them to talk to their clinician and to seek urgent care for warning signs.
I need a recruiter skill that writes job ads and structured interview plans.
help me hire people

We are a 40-person company hiring 15 people this year with no HR team. I want a skill that acts like an experienced recruiter: write inclusive job ads, define must-have versus nice-to-have criteria, build structured interviews with scoring guides, and help us give fair feedback, without ever storing or judging candidates on personal characteristics.
I want a skill that runs blameless postmortems after production incidents.
help us learn from outages

After every outage our team argues about whose fault it was and nothing changes. Build a skill that walks us step by step through a blameless postmortem: collect the timeline from logs and chat, find contributing causes with "5 whys", agree on impact, and produce action items with owners and due dates in our postmortem template.
I need a marketing strategist skill for B2B SaaS launches.
a skill to get more customers

We run a small online shop for handmade ceramics and post randomly on Instagram. I want a skill that thinks like a marketing strategist: define who our buyers are, position us against mass-produced brands, plan seasonal campaigns with a small budget, and make sure our product claims and influencer posts are honest and properly disclosed.
Build a skill that reviews NDAs before I sign them and flags risky clauses.
something that reads contracts for me

Our startup signs about ten NDAs a month with investors, partners and freelancers, and we cannot afford a lawyer for each one. I want a skill that reviews an NDA under US law, tells us whether it is mutual, flags non-competes or unusual terms hidden in it, checks the required whistleblower carve-outs, and says clearly when we need a real lawyer.
I want a skill that helps small business owners build monthly budgets and cash-flow plans.
money help for my shop

I run a small cafe with five staff and I never know if we can afford new equipment. I want a skill that builds a 12-month budget and cash-flow forecast from my sales and costs, shows the assumptions, warns me about months where cash runs short, and tells me when a question needs my accountant, especially anything about tax.
Make a skill that writes press releases for product launches and company news.
I need something for announcements

Our communications team writes about two press releases a month and they always come back from editors. I want a skill that writes them in standard press-release format (headline, dateline, lead paragraph that answers who, what, when, where and why, quotes, boilerplate, media contact), keeps them under 500 words and marks every fact we still need to confirm.
